sourceEvidence.claim: The carbapenems card: MECHANISM block (the C1-control-prefixed arrows → — the normalizer strips them)
sourceEvidence.quote:
Imipenem is a broad-spectrum, β-lactamase–
resistant carbapenem. Binds penicillin-binding
proteins →  inhibition of cell wall synthesis → 
cell death. Always administered with cilastatin
(inhibitor of renal dehydropeptidase I) to ↓
inactivation of drug in renal tubules.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: The carbapenems card: CLINICAL USE block
sourceEvidence.quote:
Gram ⊕ cocci, gram ⊝ rods, and anaerobes.
Wide spectrum and significant adverse effects
limit use to life-threatening infections or
after other drugs have failed. Meropenem
has a ↓ risk of seizures and is stable to
dehydropeptidase I.

sourceEvidence.claim: The aztreonam card: heading + MECHANISM block (the penicillinbinding hyphen-drop)
sourceEvidence.quote:
Aztreonam
MECHANISM

Less susceptible to β-lactamases. Prevents peptidoglycan cross-linking by binding to penicillinbinding protein 3. Synergistic with aminoglycosides. No cross-allergenicity with penicillins.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: The aztreonam card: CLINICAL USE block
sourceEvidence.quote:
Gram ⊝ rods only—no activity against gram ⊕ rods or anaerobes. For penicillin-allergic patients
and those with renal insufficiency who cannot tolerate aminoglycosides.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: The aztreonam card: ADVERSE EFFECTS block
sourceEvidence.quote: Usually nontoxic; occasional GI upset.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: The vancomycin card: heading + MECHANISM block
sourceEvidence.quote:
Vancomycin
MECHANISM

Inhibits cell wall peptidoglycan formation by binding D-Ala-D-Ala portion of cell wall precursors.
Bactericidal against most bacteria (bacteriostatic against C difficile). Not susceptible to
β-lactamases.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: The vancomycin card: CLINICAL USE block
sourceEvidence.quote:
Gram ⊕ bugs only—for serious, multidrug-resistant organisms, including MRSA, S epidermidis,
sensitive Enterococcus species, and C difficile (oral route).
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: The vancomycin card: ADVERSE EFFECTS block + the standalone boxed-A marker line (the line-78 'A' — the clinical photo's marker glyph)
sourceEvidence.quote:
Well tolerated in general but not trouble free: nephrotoxicity, ototoxicity, thrombophlebitis,
diffuse flushing (vancomycin infusion reaction A —idiopathic reaction largely preventable by
pretreatment with antihistamines and slower infusion rate), DRESS syndrome.

kypExtensions.summary: The pattern/trap/pivot/mini-case attack structure layered over the source facts.
kypExtensions.rationale: First Aid supplies the drug cards; the attack structure is a KYP design.

kypExtensions.summary: The four routing axes of the wall directory — tier (penicillins by beta-lactamase exposure), ladder (five cephalosporin generations with the fixed 1st-4th exclusion), escort (the four inhibitor bodyguards), and door (the 9-vs-8 split that sets the resistance route) — with the two-independent-escape-hatches reading of MRSA vs VRE.
kypExtensions.rationale: The source prints the cards as an alphabetical-adjacent directory without a routing system; the tier/ladder/escort/door axes and the escape-hatch comparison are KYP's design.
